NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Delegates must visit the neighboring settlements to settle a fishing dispute: travel together, or send one voice for all.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village and two neighboring settlements have been arguing over the same fishing grounds for a year. (subject) wants to send a delegation to each settlement, to listen first. (friend) wants one meeting with everyone at once, to settle it quickly. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) and two others spend a month paddling between the settlements, eating, listening and being shouted at. They come home with an agreement that suits everyone a little and nobody completely. It holds.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Everyone meets on a neutral beach. The meeting is loud and long, and nearly ends in a fight. In the end, they agree to share the grounds by season. Both other settlements leave feeling rushed. It holds, for now.
